114	\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%).} All nine Type~A conditions produce no significant positive effects. Even in-context learning with gold logical examples yields $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp (n.s.). Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$).
115	
116	\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%).} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning. When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.
117	
118	Four supporting analyses confirm the mechanism: constraint ablation shows MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions ($n = 804$); 91.8\% of constraints are discriminative but mirror the majority; effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($+12.8$\,pp) with direction determined by accuracy regime; and hyperparameter peaks coincide with low SC baselines (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}).

\looseness=-1 \emph{Cross-model extraction} (using a different LLM to extract constraints from the generator's traces): $\kappa$ decreases slightly but $\Delta \approx 0$, because models from the same training family share systematic biases that persist across architectures (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}).

\looseness=-1 \emph{Contrastive prompting} (eliciting pro/con constraints): produces imbalanced output (94 pro vs.\ 65 con constraints on Mistral-7B FOLIO), indicating that confirmation bias transfers from answer generation to constraint generation.

\looseness=-1 \emph{Oracle ceiling}: gold-annotated constraints yield $+29.90$\,pp (Mistral-7B FOLIO), proving the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound. Self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling, precisely localizing the bottleneck to extraction quality rather than aggregation.

\looseness=-1 All non-debate strategies cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, a same-model ceiling across three families (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}). \section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline, revealing three observation-driven accuracy regimes.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions (sorted by SC). No non-degenerate condition shows a significant gain after BH correction ($m{=}16$). $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). Symbols: $^b$gold ICL; $\dagger$\,$n < 100$; \textbf{bold}: $p < 0.05$; {*}\,uncorrected $p < 0.05$ (BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$); {***}\,oracle $p < 0.001$; $^{3s}$\,3-seed; $^{4s}$\,4-seed confirmatory (unmarked: single-seed exploratory).}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--60\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 51.00 & 51.50 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B$^{3s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 56.53 & 56.70 & $+$0.16 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 59.31 & 56.86 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 74.00 & 71.50 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\
Qwen2.5-14B$^{4s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & 74.51 & $-$0.98 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 84.80 & 84.31 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.00 & 85.67 & $+$0.67 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B (think) & FOLIO & 204 & 86.27 & 86.76 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\
QwQ-32B & AIME 2024$^\dagger$ & 22 & 72.70 & 72.70 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & GSM8K$^\dagger$ & 30 & 96.67 & 96.67 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold logical annotations + Z3)}} \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 55.88 & \textbf{85.78} & $\mathbf{+29.90}$ & $1.0{\times}10^{-13}${***} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $\mathbf{+14.22}$ & $2.0{\times}10^{-7}${***} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 74.00 & \textbf{91.17} & $\mathbf{+17.17}$ & $9.21{\times}10^{-15}${***} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\looseness=-1 No non-degenerate condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); adjusted $p = 0.112$ for both. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%) contains the only positive trends, none reaching $p < 0.05$. An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 5 positive and 10 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 0.30$, two-sided); including all conditions gives 8+/15$-$ ($p = 0.21$). Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise: two of three seeds produce null or negative $\Delta$ (mean $+0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the single-seed pattern: $\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp (mean $-1.24 \pm 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered. For the 10 underpowered conditions, our tests cannot rule out effects smaller than 1.86--4.84\,pp at 80\% power; the largest study ($n{=}804$) achieves MDE $= 1.86$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Margin sensitivity is robust: at $\pm 1$\,pp, 0/16 equivalent; at $\pm 3$\,pp, 10/16 equivalent; no margin yields a significant positive effect (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:tost-sensitivity}). We adopt $\pm 2$\,pp based on the lower bound of SC literature gains (2--5\,pp \citep{wang2023sc}), acknowledging this choice is anchored to SC effect sizes. We trace the failure below.


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

\looseness=-1 Replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations (FOLIO logical formulae, ProofWriter DSL), Oracle-SICA yields $+29.90$\,pp on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($p < 10^{-13}$), $+14.22$\,pp on Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO ($p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$), and $+17.17$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 10^{-14}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter). The MAX-SAT mechanism is sound; Mistral-7B's best self-extracted $\Delta$ ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 11.5\% of its oracle ceiling. For Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter, the gap is wider still: self-extraction degrades accuracy ($-2.50$\,pp) against an oracle ceiling of $+17.17$\,pp, indicating that stronger models do not self-extract more effectively.

On ProofWriter ($n = 600$), $w{=}3$ achieves $+6.67$\,pp ($p < 0.001$) and $w{=}5$ reaches $+11.00$\,pp ($p < 0.001$)---while same-model SICA \emph{degrades} ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:main_results}), illustrating that corrective signal must originate outside the model's distribution (\S\ref{sec:mirage}). +Three zero-cost diagnostics predict self-verification failure: $K_\text{eff} \leq 1.3$ (no condition improves), SC $< 40\%$ (constraints amplify errors; $-2.83$\,pp), and $C_0 < 5\%$ (aggregation degenerates to majority voting). Only the intermediate regime (SC $\sim$50--60\%, $K_\text{eff} > 1.8$) offers marginal gain.

-\looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints.

-\looseness=-1 Three conditions appear necessary: structural independence (no shared architecture), positive capability gap (verifier exceeds generator SC), and task-verifier alignment. These explain why 27 same-model strategies fail ($\kappa \geq 0.40$) while a 406M encoder succeeds ($+11.00$\,pp), though validation beyond propositional-logic NLI is needed. Self-verification creates a \emph{symbolic mirage}---provably sound machinery adding no information beyond majority voting---and the path forward lies in structurally independent verification, guided by $K_\text{eff}$, BR, and $C_0$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
